name: cc-enforcer
description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls — PreToolUse denies the edit before it lands, and a nine-layer Stop gate refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the original request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight of them backed by a hook; per-project "Imperial Edict" regexes you define yourself; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the docs cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.38.0 separates the languages at the source. Everything a guard PRINTS was bilingual — an English body with a Chinese plain-language line appended and Chinese phrasings offered inline — so both READMEs quoted mixed-language samples, and neither could be cleaned without either fabricating output or dropping the samples. The mixing was the product's, not the documentation's. All of that text now lives in a message catalog: `lib/messages_en.py` is the skeleton and source of truth, `lib/messages_zh.py` is its translation, and `lib/messages.py` resolves PER KEY through CC_ENFORCER_LANG, so a partial translation degrades to English rather than blanking a deny. The English half was generated mechanically from the constants the guards carried through v0.37, so the move itself could not change behaviour, and then edited so an English message names the ENGLISH spellings of the markers it describes — checked against the live pattern sets, which accept both languages, so naming only one stays true. Measured end to end: default output now contains zero CJK, and CC_ENFORCER_LANG=zh produces a fully Chinese deny across all seven deny and block paths. i18n_check gained the parity gate the markdown roots cannot have — exact key sets, per-key str.format field sets, and a check that every key a guard asks for exists at all, because a renamed key would otherwise surface as a placeholder marker inside a deny the user is already annoyed by. The status table now pads by display columns rather than code points, which only mattered once a column value could be CJK. 712 -> 733 tests. Prior — v0.37.0 fixes the boundary every hook invocation goes through: each entry point read its payload with `sys.stdin.read()`, which decodes using the HOST codepage under the `surrogateescape` error handler, so on any non-UTF-8 machine the JSON arrived silently rewritten and every guard scanned a string the agent never wrote — no exception, no stderr, no failing test. Measured on cp936, an em-dash arrived as two characters instead of one, which pushed an inline note past the rule-09 rationale floor and turned a DENY into an ALLOW: the guard was defeated by punctuation. The Stop gate had far more to lose — `大白话`, `同步核对`, `我觉得` and the done-claim patterns themselves are Chinese, so they decoded to mojibake and the CJK half of nine layers matched nothing in production. `_has_done_claim` gates all nine layers and its pattern set is bilingual, so a reply announcing completion only in Chinese matched nothing and skipped the whole stack — measured, a bare completion claim with no evidence came back allowed with not one layer having fired. Stated precisely rather than loosely, because the looser version would be the overstatement this plugin exists to block: a reply that also said "done" in ASCII still reached layer (a); what it could not do was fail on a Chinese hedge, a Chinese TL;DR marker, or a Chinese sync-check line. Same class as the v0.25 `tomlio` hardening (a wrong decode silently disabling enforcement), swept twelve releases late to the one boundary that carries every payload. Fixed at the mechanism with a new shared module, `lib/hookio.py`: read the binary buffer, decode UTF-8 strictly, and let a genuinely malformed payload raise into the existing fail-open handler — loud and diagnosable instead of quietly mangled. It survived 691 tests because the fixtures could not reach it: `tests/_helpers.py` serialised with `json.dumps`, whose `ensure_ascii=True` default escaped every non-ASCII character before the bytes existed, so the wire was pure ASCII and the decode step had nothing to get wrong. The harness now sends raw UTF-8 and a test pins that it does; the end-to-end cases force `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp936:surrogateescape` so a defect that only appears on a non-UTF-8 host still fails on the UTF-8 CI runner, with a vacuity guard that reports a stale reproduction rather than a fixed bug. Five cases verified RED against the pre-fix tree. 691 -> 712 tests. Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
